discovery: The electron recollision model of strong-field light-matter interaction and its quantum theory

nominees.name: Paul B. Corkum
nominees.affiliation: University of Ottawa and National Research Council Canada

nominees.name: Maciej Lewenstein
nominees.affiliation: ICFO - The Institute of Photonic Sciences, Barcelona

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics: strong-field and attosecond physics
motivation: Corkum's 1993 recollision picture (tunnel ionization, laser-driven acceleration, return to the parent ion) explained high-harmonic generation, above-threshold ionization plateaus and nonsequential double ionization in one simple, quantitative idea. Lewenstein and co-workers turned it into the strong-field approximation theory of harmonic generation (1994), which remains the standard framework that experimentalists and theorists use to interpret data. Recollision is the conceptual engine behind attosecond pulse generation and measurement: Corkum's proposals for attosecond streaking, molecular orbital tomography and laser-induced electron diffraction made electron motion on its natural timescale observable. The 2023 prize recognised the experimental generation of attosecond pulses; the physical understanding that made those pulses possible, and that now guides strong-field physics in molecules, solids and correlated materials, has yet to be recognised. It is a clear, testable and lasting insight into light-matter interaction.
